data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["The desert oasis has an active moisture source driving cooling, while the urban moisture deficit is a passive lack.","Oasis effects can create local cool islands rather than the persistent warm anomaly typical of UHI.","Vegetation in cities also alters albedo and sky view factor, unlike simple oasis moisture."],"overturn_conditions":["If sensible heat flux and radiative cooling dominate over latent heat flux in nocturnal urban environments.","If evapotranspiration rates after sunset are too low to meaningfully affect nocturnal cooling."],"shared_structure":["Two adjacent thermal reservoirs with different phase-change cooling potentials.","Cooling rate divergence driven by differential access to a latent heat sink."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_003"],"transfer_claims":["Just as a dry pot cools more slowly than a wet one due to lacking evaporative heat loss, an impervious city cools more slowly than vegetated countryside.","Just as adding moisture to the dry pot equalizes cooling rates, increasing urban irrigation and green space reduces the nocturnal UHI."]},"claim":"The calm, clear night UHI is driven by the rapid depletion of latent heat via evapotranspiration in the countryside, which accelerates rural cooling, while impervious urban surfaces lack moisture and cool only via slower sensible heat and longwave radiation.
